description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed completed steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. The workflow is sequential and should move quickly toward the main declared steps without unnecessary exploratory detours.
goals: Detect whether the latest agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Keep the flow sequential, simple, and consistent with the latest agent message.
Move the conversation quickly toward the main workflow steps and avoid unnecessary side exploration.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

The only step that can appear multiple times in the conversation history is `in-between-step`. All declared workflow steps — `first-hunter-intent-created`, `hunter-intent-immutability`, `hunter-card-switch`, and `hunter-questions-idempotency` — can each appear only once. If any of these steps already appears in the conversation history, it is fully consumed and must never be returned again.

After `hunter-card-switch`, do not treat the purchase receipt as the final declared step. The user's concern about a possible duplicate charge should arise only after the purchase receipt has been delivered, and the final declared step should be assigned only when the agent responds to that concern.

When all declared workflow steps have been consumed, the workflow must be considered closed. Do not reopen the flow, do not start a new purchase, and do not ask new questions. Return only a short thank-you message that closes the conversation.

step_consumption: Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest agent message.
Return a declared workflow step only if the latest agent message clearly and unambiguously starts that new declared step.

Do not assign `hunter-questions-idempotency` to the agent message that delivers the purchase receipt after `hunter-card-switch`. Assign this step only to a later agent message that directly answers or addresses the user's concern that the payment may have been processed more than once.
in_between_step_usage: If the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step, return `in-between-step`
Avoid unnecessary exploratory turns. Do not open new side topics such as brand, model, or optional preferences unless the latest agent message makes them strictly necessary to continue.
If the user has already given enough information to continue, prefer replies that move the flow forward instead of expanding the conversation.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

If the agent appears to have lost context or restarted the conversation while declared workflow steps are still active or already consumed, do not follow the agent into a new flow. Instead generate replies that bring the agent back to the active workflow context.
reply_generation: Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

When generating between 1 and 3 user replies, keep them semantically equivalent. All options must communicate the same core intent and move the workflow in the same direction, with only minor wording variation.

When the latest agent message delivers the purchase receipt after `hunter-card-switch`, generate 1 to 3 semantically equivalent user replies expressing concern about the card change and asking for confirmation that the payment was processed only once. Example: 'I am not comfortable with the card change we made. How can you assure me that the purchase was processed only once and not twice?'

steps.description: Step 1 of 4. Return this step only when the latest agent message presents the first set of concrete purchase options for the user's already confirmed initial request. At this step, NEVER select any presented option. ALL replies must reject the current offers on price and redefine the purchase intent toward a cheaper alternative product, explicitly stating no merchant preference, no specific SKU, and that refundability is not important. Preferred wording: 'These options are too expensive. I want to change my request. Please show me the cheapest basic coffee maker available, even if it is not a French press. No merchant preference, no specific SKU, and refundability is not important.'

Step 2 of 4. This step follows `first-hunter-intent-created`. Return this step when the latest agent message presents a new set of concrete purchase options based on the user's revised and confirmed request. Do not use this step for the agent message that asks the user to confirm the revised purchase details — that is `in-between-step`. Use this step only when the agent clearly presents a new numbered list of purchasable options after the revised intent was already accepted by the user. At this step, option selection is allowed.

Step 3 of 4. This step follows `hunter-intent-immutability`. Return this step when the latest agent message presents a final cart summary with a payment method already selected by the user and asks to confirm the purchase, and `hunter-card-switch` does not yet appear in the conversation history. Do not use this step when the agent is still asking the user to choose a payment method, that is `in-between-step`. Do not return this step if `hunter-card-switch` already appears in the conversation history — return `in-between-step` instead. At this step, generate replies where the user says they just remembered the other available card has a better bank offer or discount and asks to switch to that other card already shown in the flow. Do not ask to add a new card, do not ask for a different payment method outside the presented options, and do not confirm the purchase.

Step 4 of 4. This is the final declared step. It follows `hunter-card-switch`. Do not return this step when the latest agent message only delivers the purchase receipt or confirms that the transaction is complete. That receipt message is not itself this step. Return `hunter-questions-idempotency` only when the latest agent message directly answers or addresses the user's concern that the payment may have been processed more than once after the card switch. Once this step appears in the conversation history, the workflow is complete. Any later message must return `in-between-step`.
